findings.title: Intergenerational mobility fosters innovation in Europe
findings.abstract_or_evidence: The Nature article introduces EUROPE-IGM-ATLAS, annual measures of intergenerational educational mobility and educational inequality for European subnational regions over 1985–2025, based on harmonised microdata. It couples these indices to patent outcomes and uses longitudinal regional specifications and robustness checks to examine whether the relationship between educational opportunity and innovation changes across regions. The research documents European geographic disparities and a generally positive association between mobility and patenting, with weaker or heterogeneous results in historically established innovation hubs. This observational analysis cannot establish that mobility reforms alone would cause increased patenting.
principal_findings: EUROPE-IGM-ATLAS covers 225 NUTS-2 microregions or 108 NUTS-1 mesoregions in 36 European countries and includes annual measures spanning 1985–2025.

Higher intergenerational educational mobility is associated with stronger patenting outcomes across European regions over time; the association varies by starting mobility and the status of mature innovation hubs.
Observed increases in mobility are uneven across Europe and are linked largely to gains in educational attainment among people from lower-education family backgrounds.
findings.eu_ri_relevance: Direct European research-and-innovation evidence: patent-based regional innovation performance and the European distribution of opportunities to develop inventor talent.

findings.title: From green inventions to products: The role of firm and policy alignment in product integration
findings.abstract_or_evidence: This Technovation study distinguishes producing a green patented invention from integrating that invention into commercial products. Using 2,160 patent families from a European automobile manufacturer filed between 2007 and 2020, the authors examine how alignment with a firm’s established technological capabilities and with public R&D funding priorities relates to downstream product integration. The evidence indicates a stronger positive relationship for firm-capability alignment among green inventions than among non-green inventions. The study does not find clear evidence of the corresponding anticipated differential effect for policy alignment. Single-firm results should not automatically be generalized to all European industries.
principal_findings: For the 2,160 European automotive-firm patent families, stronger alignment with the firm’s previous inventive activity is more strongly associated with product integration for green inventions than non-green inventions.
The hypothesised analogous stronger relation between public R&D policy alignment and green product integration is not clearly supported.
Product integration is a distinct downstream conversion stage that cannot be inferred simply from green patent counts.
findings.eu_ri_relevance: Empirical evidence on the European private-sector R&I conversion pipeline and on how technological firm capabilities and publicly funded R&D priorities align with green innovation outcomes.
evidence_quotes: outcomes of 2160 patented inventions from a European automotive firm

findings.title: Why do Open Science policies fall short? Institutional logics and ethical framings in policy implementation in Finland
findings.abstract_or_evidence: The journal article examines Open Science policy implementation within hybrid Finnish research organisations by using a five-institutional-logics framework and survey and interview material. Rather than treating implementation as a binary question of formal compliance, it identifies ethical framings that either reinforce open research practices or obstruct them. In particular, professional and disciplinary concerns can conflict with market-oriented and managerial expectations. The author also develops a typology of researcher policy responses ranging from advocacy to alienation. The evidence describes mechanisms operating inside a European national R&I system rather than proposing generic open-science advocacy.
principal_findings: Survey and interview evidence reveals reinforcing Open Science ethical framings alongside friction between market/corporate demands and professional/disciplinary values.
Responses to Open Science mandates vary from engaged advocacy to ethical resistance and alienation, even in organisations subject to common policy goals.
Formal openness or checklist compliance need not secure data/code transparency, documentation or reproducibility.
findings.eu_ri_relevance: Direct empirical study of implementation, incentives and researcher behaviour within Finland’s research organisations, relevant to the European Research Area open-science reform agenda.

findings.title: Buyer–supplier learning under uncertainty: relational mechanisms in big science innovation procurement
findings.abstract_or_evidence: This article examines innovation-capability formation through procurement collaborations involving European Big Science organisations, intermediaries and SME suppliers in the uncertain fusion-energy research domain. It uses qualitative multiple-case research with interviews and grounded-theory analysis to identify relational foundations of organisational learning. Reported mechanisms include trust, psychological safety, open communication, joint problem-solving and knowledge exchange. In these multi-actor settings, procurement can enable supplier adaptation and both incremental and exploratory technology innovation, rather than merely transactional delivery. The findings are qualitative mechanisms, not a randomized estimate of procurement effects or a general count of economic spillovers.
principal_findings: Interviews across European big-science buyer–supplier ecosystems identify trust, psychological safety and communication as foundations for adaptive learning.
Joint problem-solving and knowledge exchange support both incremental refinement and exploration under fusion-research procurement uncertainty.
Governance of learning routines and the balance between reliable delivery and experimentation are critical for sustained inter-organisational innovation capability.
findings.eu_ri_relevance: European large research infrastructures and associated SME technology suppliers are core components of the European R&I system; this is original qualitative evidence about how infrastructure procurement develops industrial innovation capabilities.

findings.title: Assessing and comparing the coverage of publications of six Italian universities in OpenCitations
findings.abstract_or_evidence: This empirical Scientometrics study links publication records held in the IRIS current-research-information systems of six Italian universities to OpenCitations Meta and the OpenCitations Index. It matches persistent identifiers including DOI, PMID and ISBN and quantifies bibliographic and citation coverage of an open research-information infrastructure against university research output. The authors report average OpenCitations coverage above 40 percent, comparable in magnitude to figures reported elsewhere for two commercial bibliographic platforms, but considerable unevenness for social sciences and humanities formats such as monographs and critical editions. The data speak directly to limits and opportunities for responsible, transparent research evaluation in European higher education.
principal_findings: Across six Italian university IRIS CRIS installations, OpenCitations matches over 40% of publications on average.
Coverage remains unequal by output format, with particular deficiencies for SSH monographs, critical editions and associated citation metadata.
The study finds open research-information services increasingly usable for institutional evaluation, though metadata completeness and interoperability work remain necessary.

findings.title: Europe’s two towers: the uneven regional geography of telecommunication standard essential patents
findings.abstract_or_evidence: Using geocoded patent evidence, this paper maps the uneven geography of European cellular telecommunications standard-essential patents and examines regional persistence and technological change. It finds that Helsinki and Stockholm jointly account for around one-third of the European cellular standard-essential patents covered by its sample. This exceptional concentration contrasts with distributions often predicted from city population or preceding technological expertise. The authors describe positive feedback and cumulative advantage in early centres, moderated across successive telecommunications technology generations. Results are about a strategic technology and regional innovation capacity, not simply telecom market share.
principal_findings: Helsinki and Stockholm account for approximately one-third of European cellular standard-essential patents in the study.
Unlike other technologies, this patent type’s European spatial distribution is not well explained by regional population size or historical technological expertise alone.
Path-dependent early leadership appears to reinforce concentration, although technological generations can erode that advantage.
findings.eu_ri_relevance: Empirical study of European telecommunications technological leadership, regional patent concentration, standards-related innovation and competitive research capacity.
evidence_quotes: Standard Essential Patents (SEPs) in shaping technological development and regional innovation
Helsinki and Stockholm account for one-third of all cellular SEPs

findings.title: Innovation ingredients, gross domestic product and productivity: A spatial panel analysis of European regions
findings.abstract_or_evidence: The study uses spatial panel econometric models to examine links between the European Regional Innovation Scoreboard, selected disaggregated innovation attributes, GDP and productivity at European regional level. Rather than interpreting innovation investments as strictly local effects, it separates intra-regional direct associations from spillovers to nearby regions. Its models associate the aggregate RIS measure with negative contemporaneous direct effects on regional GDP/productivity but positive indirect spatial effects. Individual innovation components exhibit different sign and spillover patterns. The authors suggest potential adjustment and absorption constraints, but these mechanisms are interpretive rather than directly causal proof.
principal_findings: Across the modelled European regional panel, the aggregate Regional Innovation Scoreboard measure shows negative direct associations but positive spillover associations for productivity and GDP.
The effects of separate innovation dimensions differ; public R&D knowledge spillovers may benefit neighbouring regions even when short-term local returns are less evident.
Place-based R&I policy evaluation should track cross-border or inter-regional beneficiaries rather than assuming innovation inputs accrue only to the investing region.
findings.eu_ri_relevance: Research directly measures spatial returns, diffusion and performance of the European regional R&I system using established EU regional innovation indicators.

findings.title: Research and Innovation Careers Observatory 2026: Key Indicators on Talent, Mobility and Working Conditions
findings.abstract_or_evidence: This OECD Publishing report assembles comparative indicators about the R&I workforce using the Research and Innovation Careers Observatory (ReICO), explicitly a joint OECD–EU initiative. The official publication examines national workforce size and composition, renewal, skills, employment sectors, research careers, mobility and working conditions. It highlights previously scattered measurement of who performs research and innovation, including career sustainability and cross-border circulation. Its comparative framing supplies institutional system evidence, rather than a press item or an untested policy announcement. The direct OECD publication page records the 14 September 2026 release date and identifies OECD as the issuing body.
principal_findings: The OECD–EU Research and Innovation Careers Observatory consolidates cross-country indicators of research and innovation employment, mobility, career conditions and renewal.
The official report identifies gaps and fragmentation in existing research-workforce intelligence that constrain evidence-based national and international career policy.
The comparative framework enables policy actors to assess talent circulation and working conditions across R&I systems; country-specific causal policy effects are not claimed by this report abstract.
findings.eu_ri_relevance: An authoritative completed analytical report explicitly produced from the joint OECD–EU observatory and directly concerned with European R&I talent, research careers and mobility across systems.
